questions.q: In alkaline medium, the reduction of permanganate anion involves a gain of ____________ electrons.&
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution:
In Faintly alkaline medium potassium permanganate changes to manganese dioxide in its oxidising action.

${MnO}_{4}^{-} + 2{H}_{2}O + 3e^{-}\overset{}{→}{MnO}_{2} + 4{OH}^{-}$

The oxidation state of manganese in~${MnO}_{4}^{-}$~is +7 and in~${MnO}_{2}$& is +4.

Hence, it transfers 3 electrons during the oxidising action in alkaline medium.

questions.q:
See the following chemical reaction:

${Cr}_{2}{O}_{7}^{2 -} + {XH}^{+} + 6{Fe}^{2 +} \to {YCr}^{3 +} + 6{Fe}^{3 +} + {ZH}_{2}O$

The sum of X, Y and Z is
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution:
The given equation can be balanced using ion-electron method as shown below.

${Fe}^{2 +} \to {Fe}^{3 +} + e^{-}$~ ~ ~ ~ ~-oxidation Half reaction

$6e^{-} + 14H^{+} + {Cr}_{2}{O}_{7}^{2 -} \to 2{Cr}^{3 +} + 7{H}_{2}O$~-Reduction Half reaction

The overall reaction is~

$6{Fe}^{2 +} + 14H^{+} + {Cr}_{2}{O}_{7}^{2 -} \to 6{Fe}^{3 +} + 2{Cr}^{3 +} + 7{H}_{2}O$

The values~$X = 14, Y = 2andZ = 7$

$( X + Y + Z ) = 14 + 2 + 7$

$= 23$

questions.q:
$2{MnO}_{4}^{-} + {bC}_{2}{O}_{4}^{2 -} + {cH}^{+} \to {xMn}^{2 +} + {yCO}_{2} + {zH}_{2}O$
If the above equation is balanced with integer coefficients, the value of $c$& is _______ . (Round off to the Nearest Integer).
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution:
Writing the half reaction

Reduction half reaction&

${MnO}_{4}^{-} \to {Mn}^{2 +}$

balancing oxygen~

${MnO}_{4}^{-} \to {Mn}^{2 +} + 4{H}_{2}O$

balancing Hydrogen~

$8H^{+} + {MnO}_{4}^{-} \to {Mn}^{2 +} + 4{H}_{2}O$

balancing charge~

$5e^{-} + 8H^{+} + {MnO}_{4}^{-} \to {Mn}^{2 +} + 4{H}_{2}O$

Oxidation half~

${C}_{2}{O}_{4}^{2 -} \to {CO}_{2}$
Balancing carbon

${C}_{2}{O}_{4}^{2 -} \to 2{CO}_{2}$

Balancing charge

${C}_{2}{O}_{4}^{2 -} \to 2{CO}_{2} + 2e^{-}$

Net equation

$16H^{+} + 2{MnO}_{4}^{-} + 5{C}_{2}{O}_{4}^{2 -} \to 10{CO}_{2} + 2{Mn}^{2 +} + 8{H}_{2}O$

So $c = 16$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution:
Complete acid is not used in the reaction.

Milli eq. of ${NH}_{3} =$~milli eq. of~$NaOH$

$= 0 . 25 \times 30$

$= 7 . 5$

Millimole of Nitrogen~$= 7 . 5$

${W}_{Nitrogen} = 7 . 5 \times 14 \times {10}^{- 3}$

$= 0 . 105gram$

$%$of Nitrogen~$= \dfrac{0 . 105}{0 . 166} \times 100 = 63 . 25 = 63$

questions.q: $20mL$~of calcium hydroxide was consumed when it was reacted with $10mL$ of unknown solution of ${H}_{2}{SO}_{4} .$ Also $20mL$ standard solution of $0 . 5MHCl$ containing $2$ drops of phenolphthalein was titrated with calcium hydroxide, the mixture showed pink colour when burette displayed the value of $35 . 5mL$ whereas the burette showed $25 . 5mL$ initially. The concentration of ${H}_{2}{SO}_{4}$~is _______M .& (Nearest integer)
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution:
Titration principle is& ${N}_{1}{V}_{1} = {N}_{2}{V}_{2}$

N = Normality

V = Volume of solution

${M}_{1}{V}_{1}{n}_{1} = {M}_{2}{V}_{2}{n}_{2}$

M = molarity

n = Valence factor of acid or base

As pink colour is obtained on consumption of $10ml$~of $Ca ( OH{)}_{2},$ we have

$20 \times 0 . 5 \times 1 = 10 \times M \times 2$

Molarity of~$Ca ( OH{)}_{2} = \dfrac{10}{20} = \dfrac{1}{2}M$

Also, moles of~$Ca ( OH{)}_{2} = mm$~of~${H}_{2}{SO}_{4}$

$\dfrac{1}{2} \times 20 = 10 \times M$

Molarity of~${H}_{2}{SO}_{4} = 1M$

questions.q:
$2{MnO}_{4}^{-} + {bI}^{-} + {cH}_{2}O \to {xI}_{2} + {yMnO}_{2} + {zOH}^{-}$

If the above equation is balanced with integer coefficients, the value of $z$ is ________.
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution:
Reduction Half reaction

$2{MnO}_{4}^{-} \to 2{MnO}_{2}$

$2{MnO}_{4}^{-} + 4{H}_{2}O + 6e^{-} \to 2{MnO}_{2} + 8{OH}^{-}$

Oxidation Half reaction

$2I^{-} \to {I}_{2} + 2e^{-}$

$6I^{-} \to 3{I}_{2} + 6e^{-}$

Adding oxidation half and reduction half, net reaction is

$2{MnO}_{4}^{-} + 6I^{-} + 4{H}_{2}O \to 3{I}_{2} + 2{MnO}_{2} + 8{OH}^{-}$

$⇒ z = 8$

$⇒ Ans8$

questions.q: The normality of ${H}_{2}{SO}_{4}$ in the solution obtained on mixing $100mL$ of $0 . 1M{H}_{2}{SO}_{4}$ with $50mL$ of $0 . 1MNaOH$ is____\times {10}^{- 1}N.
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution:
No. of equivalents of& ${H}_{2}{SO}_{4} = M \times V \times n - factor = 100 \times 0 . 1 \times 2 = 20$

No. of equivalents of~$NaOH = 50 \times 0 . 1 = 5$

No. of equivalents of ${H}_{2}{SO}_{4}$ left~$= 20 - 5 = 15$

$⇒ 150 \times x = 15$

$x = \dfrac{1}{10} = 0 . 1N = 1 \times {10}^{- 1}N$

questions.q: If $50mL$ of $0 . 5M$ oxalic acid is required to neutralise $25mL$ of $NaOH$ solution, the amount of $NaOH$ in $50mL$ of given $NaOH$ solution is_______g.
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution:
$50$ml of $0 . 5M$ oxalic acid is completely neutralised by $25$ml of $NaOH$ solution.

For neutralisation reactions, ${N}_{1}{V}_{1} = {N}_{2}{V}_{2}$

Normality of oxalic acid = Molarity$\times2$

$⇒ {N}_{oxalicacid} = 0 . 5 \times 2 = 1N$

$50 \times 1 = 25 \times {N}_{NaOH}$

For sodium hydroxide, molarity is the same as normality.

Molarity of sodium hydroxide = $2$M

The number of moles of sodium hydroxide= $50 \times 2 \times {10}^{- 3}mol$.

Hence, the mass of sodium hydroxide $= 50 \times 2 \times {10}^{- 3} \times 40 = 4g$

questions.q: $20mL$ of $0 . 02{MK}_{2}{Cr}_{2}{O}_{7}$ solution is used for the titration of $10mL$ of ${Fe}^{2 +}$ solution in the acidic medium. The molarity of ${Fe}^{2 +}$ solution is____\times {10}^{- 2}M
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution:
Equivalents of ${K}_{2}{Cr}_{2}{O}_{7} =$ Equivalents of~${Fe}^{2 +}$

$⇒$(Molarity $\times$ volume $\timesn . f$) of ${K}_{2}{Cr}_{2}{O}_{7} =$ (molarity $\times$ volume $\times$~$n . f$)~of~${Fe}^{2 +}$

$n . f = n - factor ( valencefactor )$

$⇒ 0 . 02 \times 20 \times 6 = M \times 10 \times 1$

$⇒ M = 0 . 24$

$⇒$ Molarity~$= 24 \times {10}^{- 2}$

questions.q: The density of a monobasic strong acid (Molar mass $24 . 2gmol )$ is $1 . 21kgL$. The volume of its solution required for the complete neutralization of $25mL$ of $0 . 24MNaOH$ is ${10}^{- 2}mL$ (Nearest integer)
questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.solution:
millimole of $NaOH = 0 . 24 \times 25$
For nuetralisation, equal moles~of monoacidic base and monobasic acid must be present:

$∴$ millimole of acid $= 0 . 24 \times 25$

$⇒$ mass of acid $= 0 . 24 \times 25 \times 24 . 2g$

for pure acid,

$V = \dfrac{w}{d}; ( d = 1 . 21kg / L = 1 . 21g / ml )$

$∴ V = \dfrac{0 . 24 \times 25 \times 24 . 2}{1 . 12} \times {10}^{- 3}$

$= 120 \times {10}^{- 3}ml$

$= 12 \times {10}^{- 2}ml$
